cards.title: Introduction to Props
cards.content:
Props are custom attributes you can register on a component. When a value is passed to a prop attribute, it becomes a property on that component instance.

Data flows strictly downward: from parent to child.

cards.title: Defining Props in Composition API
cards.content:
In Vue 3 with <script setup>, props are defined using the defineProps() macro.

<script setup>
defineProps({
  title: String,
  likes: Number
})
</script>

cards.title: Prop Validation
cards.content:
Vue components can define requirements for their props. If a requirement is met, Vue will warn you in the browser console. This is especially useful when authoring a component that is intended to be used by others.

defineProps({
  age: {
    type: Number,
    required: true,
    validator(value) {
      return value >= 0
    }
  }
})

cards.title: Best Practices for Props
cards.content:
Remember the golden rule: Props are read-only (unidirectional).

Never mutate a prop directly inside a child component. If you need to modify prop data locally, define a local ref or computed property instead.
